subject: Reconciling peak burst windows & steady-state for dedicated commit — data request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reconciling peak burst windows & steady-state for dedicated commit — data request

Alex —

Following up on the LumenAI sizing call: to get a tight Dedicated commit estimate we need a small set of telemetry artifacts from your side. If you can drop the CSV and a couple sample sessions we can map to GPU SKUs, batching and caching assumptions. Minimal set below — the fields are intentionally focused (1–2 hours of sample across a typical weekday and your largest single-burst event):

- 1-min and 5-min peak concurrent requests (time-series)
- Per-request prompt tokens and response tokens (histogram or sample rows)
- Typical session duration and fraction of multi-turn sessions (session_id + length)
- % of requests that reuse KV cache (same conversation/session) vs cold-start
- Expected p50/p95 latency SLO target for gen requests (ms) and whether p99 tail matters for UX
- Model variants in play (e.g., open-7b-q4, redwood-13b-fp16), and whether you can accept quantized variants for cost savings
- Dayparting / timezone peaks (UTC offset) — does traffic concentrate in a 2–3 hour window or is it distributed?
- Any hard constraints (air-gapped data, retention windows, maximum allowable token retention)

If possible please include: a small sample CSV (schema: timestamp, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, model, cold_start_bool, trace_id) and a handful of full session JSONs for inspection.

Attachment: lumen_peak_sample.csv (CSV stub)

Goal: with these we can produce 3 scenarios — conservative commit, expected commit, and 2x burst capacity — and show cost/latency trade-offs + recommended GPU mix.

Can you send the artifacts by Monday so we can scope the dedicated sizing before contract reviews? Also flag procurement contact if PO will be required to hold any reserved capacity.

Thanks,

— Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@lumenai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenai.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 13:45:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Reconciling peak burst windows & steady-state for dedicated commit — data request

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Attached is a first pass: token_distribution_sample.csv and two session dumps (one retail workload, one support-chat workload). High level notes:

- Typical weekday baseline: ~120 rps sustained (UTC-7) with a 10–12 minute peak in the morning that can spike to ~1.6k rps for a 7–10 minute marketing-triggered event.
- Prompt tokens: median 38, mean 72 (long tail to ~2k). Response tokens: median 64, mean 140.
- Cold-starts are ~18% of requests; long-lived sessions (multi-turn > 5 turns) represent ~9% of traffic but account for ~35% of token volume.
- Current model mix: open-7b-q4 for light endpoints, redwood-13b-fp16 for higher quality flows; willingness to test q4 variants for 13b if latency improves.
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for most endpoints; p99 can be relaxed to 1.2s for background flows.

We are attaching the CSVs now. Procurement looped in on the cc — they will likely start a PO process after sizing.

Attachments: token_distribution_sample.csv, support_sessions_retail.json

— Alex
Lead Platform Engineer, LumenAI
alex.wu@lumenai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reconciling peak burst windows & steady-state for dedicated commit — data request

On Sat, Jul 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex —
> 
> Following up on the LumenAI sizing call: to get a tight Dedicated commit estimate we need a small set of telemetry artifacts from your side.

Thanks — this looks good and the samples are exactly the type we want. A couple of follow-ups so we can map to GPU SKUs and batching knobs:

- Please give the 95th and 99th percentile sequence lengths (prompt + response) per endpoint. We need those to size KV cache and memory headroom — average alone will understate memory.
- For the spike event, can you tell us if the 1.6k rps spike is sustained across many endpoints or concentrated on one route (e.g., /recommendations)? If concentrated, we can propose sharding by route with different GPU SKUs.
- Share a small tracer sample (trace_id column) for a handful of p95 requests that includes timing breakdown (ingest, batching queue, model_token_emit).
- Tell us whether you currently route different user tiers to different model variants or use a single variant per endpoint.

We'll run the inputs through the Dedicated Sizer (internal) and produce three artifacts: 1) a recommended fleet mix (GPU SKUs + count), 2) expected monthly cost delta vs hosted, and 3) a canary rollout plan with fallback model variants.

Attachment: redwood_qna_checklist.pdf (PDF stub)

Marissa
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@lumenai.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reconciling peak burst windows & steady-state for dedicated commit — data request

Marissa / Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement will initiate a PO thread this week (they asked for the expected monthly headline number to include in the justification). We can schedule the technical deep-dive on Friday (your availability?) to walk through the sample sessions and the canary/retry behavior.

Quick answers: the 1.6k spike is concentrated on /mobile-recs; we currently route light users to open-7b-q4 and logged-in users to the 13b; we'll extract p95/p99 seq lengths and tracer snippets and drop them in the Drive link by Thursday.

Thanks — Alex
